items.title: Louis Armstrong Interview, 1961-02-10
items.q: Anywhere Joe Glazer sent me. I'll go.

ctx.x: Yeah. During these trips that you take, for example, well, wherever it is, Sweden, Africa, what are some of the questions that people ask you?

Well, what kind of food and what's happening in America, what they've cast during. There's a lot of trumpet players that are very good and perfect on instruments. We'd like to come to the States and show how good they can play. And I told them, I'll see Mr. Glazer. Maybe you can have some of them come over to go to school and come back and make bands and different things.

items.title: Louis Armstrong Interview, 1960-08-16
items.q: I went into the front set with Carol Dickerson's orchestra which was owned by Joe Glazer, my manager

ctx.x: working with men that are better than you and I guess there was a time when there was someone better than you when you were awfully young.

All of my life in music and whatever happened to me right today comes from observing some of the musicians that were playing something. And I was always lucky to play with good musicians. When I went into Chicago I was sitting with Joe, Johnny Dots, Baby Dots and all of them good. Leo on piano and Joe Arroyo and Lauren at Horn. I said, why didn't we do it? Now, I went into the front set with Carol Dickerson's orchestra which was owned by Joe Glazer, my manager, and Joe Glazer and Joe Rollins who was called the…
I wouldn't listen to it. I've noticed you've talked a lot about Joe Oliver, and he must have been a tremendous influence.

items.title: Louis Armstrong: Jazz Casual Interview, 1964-07-10
items.q: And then I went into the Sunset with Joe Glazer in 1926.

ctx.x: We both was using cornets, you know. Well now when you went in to make a record day like Snake Rag, had you been playing this tune? Had he been, had he been? Not this one. Yeah.

It's one of them he made up for the Ginette record. When he started making records then he started being a writer. Yeah. And that stuff would come up later, you know. Would you rehearse that then in the studio before you recorded it? Well we'd rehearse that on the job, you know. Uh-huh. And then by the time we'd get to the studio all they'd do is cut it up and time it to, yeah. Yeah. Yeah. For no trouble at all, you know, to make them records, because they'd make one after another. It wasn't as particular as it…
Now you spoke before about how they didn't have the drums. Baby Dodds just played Woodblocks. Uh, that daughter's baby was there.
